name: all_n_reads
mechanism: A FASTQ file where every base in every read is called as N (the IUPAC ambiguity code for 'any base') is submitted to analysis tools. This occurs in practice when: a basecaller fails and outputs all-N sequences rather than erroring, a truncated file is padded with N characters by a downstream processor, or an upstream format conversion step corrupts the base calls. N bases contribute no valid k-mers (they match nothing exactly), produce no seeds in alignment tools, and trigger no peaks in de Bruijn graph construction. Tools that count reads will see a non-zero read count — the file is not empty — but the reads carry zero biological information. Most tools map 0% of reads and produce empty output with exit 0, with no distinction between 'no reads aligned because the organism is wrong' and 'no reads aligned because the reads are uninformative N sequences'.

known_behaviors.behavior: All reads unmapped (flag 0x4). MAPQ=0 for all reads. Paired-mate rescue may place mate reads at MAPQ=0 positions. Exit 0, valid BAM.
Produces 0 contigs. BayesHammer error correction removes all-N reads. Exit 0. No warning that input was degenerate.
Reports 100% N content in 'Per Base Sequence Quality' and 'Per Base N Content' modules. Flags FAIL. One of the few tools that detects this condition — but does not prevent downstream use.

download.command: datasets download genome accession GCF_000006945.2 --include genome --filename genome.zip && unzip -q genome.zip && cat ncbi_dataset/data/GCF_000006945.2/*.fna > assembly.fasta && rm -rf ncbi_dataset genome.zip README.md

samples.description: 1000 read pairs of 150bp, all bases N, quality scores all I (Phred 40) — valid FASTQ format, zero biological information

recipe.description: Generate 1000 paired-end FASTQ records where every base is N and every quality score is I (Phred+33=40). Valid FASTQ format with non-zero read count.
recipe.command:
python3 -c "
import gzip
def make_reads(path, count=1000, length=150):
    with gzip.open(path, 'wt') as f:
        for i in range(count):
            f.write(f'@read_{i}/1\n')
            f.write('N' * length + '\n')
            f.write('+\n')
            f.write('I' * length + '\n')
make_reads('reads_1.fq.gz')
make_reads('reads_2.fq.gz')
"

download.command: echo 'n_reads is recipe-based; run acquire.py to generate'

curation.notes: Quality scores are set to I (Phred 40) so the reads pass quality filtering — the failure is in the base content, not the quality. This is important: a tool that pre-filters on quality would correctly discard low-quality reads but will pass these N-reads through to alignment/assembly.
